items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the navigation law, in relation to the creation of a Hudson River pilots surcharge board; and to amend the navigation law, in relation to time restrictions on continuous pilotage on vessels transiting the Hudson River
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3951

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the navigation law, in relation to the creation of a
Hudson River pilots surcharge board; and to amend the navigation law,
in relation to time restrictions on continuous pilotage on vessels
transiting the Hudson River

PURPOSE:

To establish a surcharge on vessels piloted by the Hudson River Pilots
for the purpose of creating a pension fund for retired Hudson River
Pilots.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section two of the bill amends the Navigation Law § 89-a (4) (b) (1)
to add a new subdivision (ii) to establish a surcharge on every
foreign and American vessel under navigating the waters of the Hudson
River including Section 1 (Lower River - Yonkers to all ports through
Hyde Park) and Section 2 (Upper River - Yonkers to all ports beyond
Hyde Park through Albany or Troy). The charges will increase to a
stated amount every twelve months for four years.

Section three is amended to create a Hudson River pilots surcharge
board to determine the rate of the surcharge that will be levied in
addition to the base surcharge in order to fund the retirement
benefits for Hudson River pilots on a sound actuarial basis. The
additional surcharge will be raised to a set amount every twelve
months until sixty months have passed, at which point the Hudson River
pilots surcharge board will determine its amount using actuarial
principles and not allowing it to exceed 35 percent of the sum of base
pilotage charges or $5,000 in a calendar year. Retirement benefits
accumulating from the additional surcharge will pay a yearly
retirement benefit to currently active Hudson River pilots, retired
Hudson River pilots, and eligible surviving spouses of retired pilots.

JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, pensions of retired Hudson River Pilots are financed out of
annual revenues and determined by active pilot earnings. This current
pension system creates an unfunded pension liability. This legislation
is intended to correct the unfunded liability and replace it with an
actuarially sound system. Sandy Hook Pilots already have legislation
in place that has successfully accomplished a strengthening of their
pension system. With a shortage of pilots on the Hudson River, a
stronger pension may reward and encourage those who put the effort
into becoming pilots.

The current pilotage tariff will continue to cover all operational
expenses and distribution to active pilots. This till does not grant
an increase in earnings to active pilots. The legislation will
establish a pension surcharge to be determined by the Hudson River
pilots surcharge board. The surcharge will be monitored quarterly by
the Surcharge Board and adjusted as necessary to cover the pensions of
retired pilots.


LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2013-2014: A.7912 - Referred to Transportation

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become law.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 11 Chapter 478

       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 3951-B, entitled:

    "AN  ACT to amend the navigation law, in relation to the creation of
        a Hudson River pilots surcharge board; and to amend the  naviga-
        tion  law,  in relation to time restrictions on continuous pilo-
        tage on vessels transiting the Hudson River"

    APPROVED

  This bill would amend the Navigation Law  to  create  a  Hudson  River
pilots  surcharge board to determine the rate of the surcharge that will
be levied, in addition to the base  surcharge,  in  order  to  fund  the
retirement benefits for Hudson River pilots on a sound actuarial basis.

  However, the version of this bill passed by the Legislature removed an
important  amendment  to the Navigation Law that would have changed time
restrictions on continuous pilotage on  vessels  transiting  the  Hudson
River.  That  change  would  have reflected the actual time it typically
takes to pilot a vessel from Yonkers to the Port of Albany. The Legisla-
ture has agreed to pass legislation in the upcoming  session  to  remedy
this concern, and on that basis, I will approve this bill.

  The bill is approved.                       (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
